The most important of those votes was the one on the Gold Initiative. Had the initiative passed, the Swiss National Bank would have been required to hold at least 20% of its balance sheet in gold. This would have shackled the Bank, ending its efforts to tie the Swiss Franc to the Euro, and regaining for the Swiss people the advantages of a strong currency.

Early opinion polls suggested strong popular support for this enlightened measure. Sadly, but entirely predictably, the anti-gold propaganda effort mobilized by the Switzerland's political and media establishment was enough to dupe the masses into voting against their own interests, and so the measure was defeated.
